summary: FFLA lists a standing open tower called Pine Ridge in Clinton County; OSM tags the same spot as Flat Rock Fire Tower, a lattice observation tower. Private; no build date.

access.note: The FFLA's April 2022 newsletter calls the Pine Ridge tower near Altona private. The Almanack says access to the Flat Rock area is by permit managed by Miner Institute.

visit.trail_note: No public visiting route found. The Almanack says access to the Flat Rock area is by permit.

events.note: Altona Flat Rock fire, August 1957, described as the worst in New York State in more than a decade. A game warden had often used a 20-foot tower on the central Flat Rock; the article does not say whether it is the structure FFLA lists.

corrections.why: The FFLA list types this site as an Open Tower, not a platform. OpenStreetMap tags the same spot as an observation tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA list calls the site Pine Ridge; OpenStreetMap calls the tower at the same coordinates Flat Rock Fire Tower. The story treats them as one structure, which the sources suggest but do not confirm.
The 2022 newsletter calls the tower private. The Almanack says the Flat Rock area is under a permit system. Recorded as private, with the permit note.

notes_for_editor: Only four sources, and the Pine Ridge name appears only in the FFLA list. The OpenStreetMap node matches the FFLA coordinates, and the Almanack photo credit names an Altona Flat Rock Fire Tower, but no source ties the three names to one structure. The 1957 tower on the central Flat Rock is not linked to this site. Record kind 'platform' is proposed as 'tower'. Almanack photo credits have no image URLs, so no photos were added.
